Subject: Data residency & VPC options for ClearHealth - initial ask

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We are starting procurement for a conversational assistant that will process patient-facing metadata and some pseudonymized health records. Before we proceed to technical validation, our Legal & Security teams need clarity on a few points around data residency and tooling:

- Can Redwood guarantee EU-only processing and storage for ClearHealth workloads (both tokens and logs)?
- Do you offer a VPC/private deployment (customer VPC or on-prem connector) with customer-controlled KMS?
- Please share SOC2 evidence, SIG/CAIQ responses (or a link), and your standard DPA with SCCs.
- Anything Redwood can provide to help our DPIA (data flow diagrams, retention controls, deletion procedures).

Could you attach the SOC2 report and a pointer to SIG/CAIQ artifacts? If a VPC option exists, we need a short description of the hosting model and whether traffic ever leaves the EU region.

Objective: get artifacts this week so our legal can triage for the procurement packet.

Thank you,
Anna
Anna Schmidt
Head of IT Security
ClearHealth GmbH

Subject: RE: Data residency & VPC options for ClearHealth - initial ask

Anna,

Appreciate the clear list — happy to help and copied Marcus (security) and Marissa (solutions) to provide the artifacts and technical detail. Short answers up front:

- EU-only: yes — our hosted service supports region locking to EU cloud regions and we can configure project-level routing so ClearHealth traffic is processed and stored in EU-only partitions.
- VPC/private: we offer Redwood Private (VPC + customer-managed control plane) and a Dedicated option; both support customer KMS integration. For the strictest separation we recommend Redwood Private in a customer VPC with optional on-prem connector.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II, completed SIG questionnaire, and CAIQ notes are available. I will share the SOC2 PDF and a Drive folder with SIG/CAIQ.
- DPIA support: we can supply redacted data flow diagrams, retention controls, and a short DPIA template noting our processing activities for Common Use Cases.

Marcus — can you attach the SOC2 PDF and a link to the SIG/CAIQ folder? Also, please include a short note on KMS and cross-border egress. Marissa — can you draft a 1-page summary for the DPA + SCCs and a tentative MAP (mutual action plan) for procurement timelines?

Proposed cadence: I'll send artifacts today; if helpful we can schedule a 30-minute security sync with your DPO and our security team.

Best,
Evelyn

Anna / Evelyn,

Attaching the high-level artifacts you requested and a short technical note. See attachments and links below:

Attachments (stubs):

- Redwood_Private_VPC_Overview.pdf (architecture diagram and KMS integration patterns)

Links (read-only):

- DPA (template with SCCs): https://drive.google.com/file/d/REDWOOD-DPA-TEMPLATE

Technical notes:
- Hosting: In Redwood Private the inference hosts and persistent storage are deployed into the customer's VPC (or dedicated VPC peering) in the selected cloud region. Control plane connectivity is via mutually authenticated TLS; metadata necessary for operational governance can be configured to remain in-region.
- KMS: Customer-managed KMS is supported (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS). The model keys / encryption keys for long-term storage can be configured to use customer key encryption. Ephemeral keys used for in-memory inference are not stored persistently.
- Egress & logs: By default, telemetry and aggregated metrics are retained in-region; operational alerts that require cross-region routing can be disabled. Access to raw request payload logs is configurable and can be disabled entirely for a given tenant.
- DPIA support: We can provide redacted dataflow diagrams (request → inference → result), retention policy statements, and sample deletion playbooks for inclusion in your DPIA. Typical turnaround for a short DPIA bundle is 3–5 business days.

Let me know if you need specific answers for subprocessors (we publish the list in our DPA) or if you want an exportable artifact for your DPIA.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

1) KMS detail: can you confirm that customer keys never leave the customer-controlled KMS and that Redwood has no ability to export plaintext keys? We need this explicitly in the DPA.
2) Subprocessor list: please confirm which cloud regions and subprocessor identities will be listed in the DPA for an EU-only commitment.
3) Can you share a short statement on retention: default log retention, and the ability to implement tenant-level retention/deletion policies? We need a bullet we can paste into our DPIA.

We also want to schedule a 30-min security convene this week (DPO + Head of IT Security + Redwood security). Our availability: Wed 9 Sep, 14:00–16:00 CEST or Fri 11 Sep, 10:00–12:00 CEST.

Best,
Anna

Anna — thanks for the questions and for proposing times. Wed 9 is now passed, but Fri 11 Sep at 10:30 CEST works for our security and infra leads (we had to shuffle a couple of calendars). I've booked a 30-minute slot and included a brief MAP and next steps attachment.

Quick answers to your numbered items:
1) KMS: confirmed — customer-managed KMS keys remain under customer control. Redwood does not have the ability to export customer-managed KMS plaintext keys. We'll add explicit language to the DPA + KMS rider.
2) Subprocessors: we will provide a finalized EU-only subprocessors list in the DPA. Typically this includes the cloud region provider (e.g., AWS eu-west-1) and select managed backup/storage services; we will mark anything outside EU as not used for this engagement.
3) Retention: default log retention for request traces is 30 days; tenant-level retention policies can be implemented down to 0 days for raw request payloads. We will provide a one-paragraph retention statement for your DPIA.
